rankings.blurb: Eleven Cornerstones and Foundational pieces. ELEVEN. While everyone else is scraping together pick pyramids and praying on rookies, Sven is sitting on Ja'Marr Chase, JSN, Jayden Daniels, De'Von Achane, and Omarion Hampton like a dragon on a pile of gold. The WR room alone would make grown men weep — three Cornerstones across the board. Yes, the recent trades have been bleeding value left and right, and the pick cupboard is nearly bare, but when your floor is this high, you can afford to take a few punches. The Swenvengers are the class of this league until further notice.

Four Cornerstones including the Gibbs-Maye-Nacua-McBride holy quad is absolutely filthy — this roster reads like a fantasy fever dream. Ekleiner overpaid for Gibbs in a technical sense but let's be real, getting a top-3 dynasty RB even at a slight premium is a win when your window is open right now. The Achilles heel here is the pick situation — one lonely first-round pick is basically a participation trophy in a league full of pick hoarders. Depth behind the stars gets thin fast, and if Kyren Williams or Jonathon Brooks can't deliver, the RB2 spot becomes a problem. Still, this roster wins today AND in two years, and that's a rare thing.

Seven first-round picks and Caleb Williams as your anchor — Jsinykin is playing dynasty chess while everyone else plays checkers. The Trey McBride trade looks like a W in hindsight, collecting a mountain of picks while reloading with Jeremiyah Love and Jaxson Dart as the young core. The WR room is stacked with upside in Egbuka, Olave, and Luther Burden, which is a genuinely scary trio for years to come. The concern is the current gap between 'upside' and 'production' — this team has eight Upside Premier players and only one Cornerstone, meaning you're betting on a lot of guys to hit. But with that pick war chest, Siny can buy anyone who does hit, and that's terrifying.

Josh Allen alone justifies a top-five placement — the man is the single highest KTC player in this entire league at 9,998 and he's YOUR guy, Gavin. Pairing him with Ashton Jeanty, Bo Nix, James Cook, and a Foundational WR trio of Wilson/Flowers/Waddle is a roster that can compete right now and reload simultaneously. The recent Shough-for-Garrett Wilson swap was a loss on paper but Garrett Wilson is a real player and Shough is a dart throw, so the optics are fine. The TE room is the glaring weakness — Sam LaPorta as your starter in a TE premium league is a liability. Overall though, this is a team with a legitimate superstar QB and enough surrounding talent to be dangerous every single season.

Zero first-round picks. Zero. You traded away two 2027 firsts to Siny for BREECE HALL, and then you got fleeced by nchernandez for Jameson Williams and two future firsts in exchange for basically nothing tangible. GiantHawkTua is out here fumbling the bag in real time while sitting on a legitimately good core of Burrow, Amon-Ra, Hurts, and Jonathan Taylor. The window is open, the talent is real, but the pick-stripping is going to hurt badly when this aging core starts to decline. Tyler Warren is a genuine upside play at TE which is nice, but Breece Hall as RB1 is a shaky foundation. This team is one Burrow injury away from a five-alarm crisis with no draft capital to rebuild.

Bijan Robinson and Brock Bowers as your two Cornerstones is a genuinely elite foundation — the problem is the supporting cast looks like a CFL practice squad. Jordan Love is a real QB1 but CJ Stroud as your backup is more prayer than plan. Nchernandez has been an absolute SHARK in trades recently — fleecing SvenMoney34 and GiantHawkTua for a haul of picks that now has six first-rounders stacked up. The WR room featuring Marvin Harrison and Jameson Williams has swing-for-the-fences upside but is currently producing nothing. If even two of those six firsts become useful starters alongside Bijan and Bowers, this team legitimately contends in 2027-28. For now, they're a high-upside rebuild that's been winning the trade table.

Look, the Dynastyze ranking has this team at dead last with 28.4K, but the data here tells a more interesting story — five first-round picks and a trade record that reads like a highlight reel. Selling Gibbs back to ekleiner for a pick haul was the deal of the offseason, full stop. The problem is the current roster is genuinely rough — Tyler Shough as QB1, TreVeyon Henderson and Jadarian Price as your RB core, and George Kittle on a walker as your short-term TE band-aid. Travis Hunter is a name to watch but this team is two to three years away from competing. The pick capital is real though, and Seth is clearly not afraid to wheel and deal, so don't sleep on this rebuild.

Congrats on selling Ja'Marr Chase — truly the boldest 'blow it all up' moment of the offseason. Seven first-round picks is impressive until you realize you traded the best wide receiver in dynasty to get there, and now your current WR1 is Malik Nabers on an island with Quentin Johnston and Jalen Coker as the supporting cast. Fernando Mendoza as a QB1 dart throw is either genius or a disaster waiting to happen, and Bhayshul Tuten at RB isn't inspiring anyone. The pick capital is real and the rebuild vision is clear, but this roster is genuinely uncompetitive for at least two years. The Skyline Chili of dynasty rosters — some people love it, most people are confused by it.

Jefferson and CeeDee Lamb as your top two is a genuinely baller WR duo, but everything else on this roster is held together with duct tape and vibes. Brock Purdy, Jared Goff, and Sam Darnold as your QB room is the most aggressive median-chasing QB strategy in league history. The RB situation is a ticking clock — McCaffrey is a Short-term Winner which is just a polite way of saying 'enjoy it while it lasts,' and Saquon Barkley is in the same boat. One pick owned, zero future planning, and a recent trade record that features losing value to Herschey of all people. This window is closing faster than Grey realizes, and there's no draft capital to reopen it.

Lamar Jackson AND Patrick Mahomes as your QB1 and QB2 is an absolutely unhinged flex — truly the most expensive luxury problem in dynasty football. The issue is literally everything else: Derrick Henry and Travis Kelce as short-term production pieces, zero future picks owned, and a RB room of Josh Jacobs and Tony Pollard that would make a grown man cry. Herschey traded away a 2028 first to get Ladd McConkey — a nice player, but that's your ONLY first and you have no picks at all in your war chest. This team is one Lamar hamstring away from a complete catastrophe with no lifeline. The dual-QB kings are dynasty dead men walking, and the championship window is approximately one season wide.
